html:
The Botai culture was a people of the north Kazakh steppe who lived from about 3500 to 3000 BCE, in villages of pit houses, and depended almost wholly on horses.

At Botai itself, archaeologists found hundreds of thousands of horse bones, and traces of mare's milk fats in pots. Wear on some teeth may come from bits, a sign of riding. That made Botai a strong candidate for the first tamed horses.

DNA studies since 2018 have complicated the story: the Botai horses were the ancestors of Przewalski's horses, not of today's domestic breeds, which came from the western steppe later. Even so, Botai shows people on the steppe living off horses very early. Horses, mare's milk and the riding life later made the steppe the home of Scythians, Turks and Kazakhs.
sum: The Botai culture was a people of the north Kazakh steppe who lived from about 3500 to 3000 BCE, in villages of pit houses, and depended almost wholly on horses.
